subject: art-design
title: Painting Techniques: Application
welcome_lead: Apply named techniques — wet-on-wet, impasto, glazing — and build coherent palettes.
meta_desc: Applying GCSE painting techniques: wet-on-wet, impasto, glazing, limited palette.
final_note: Named techniques give you a language to plan.

concepts.def: Adding wet paint into a wet area to blend.
Using little paint on a dry brush for texture.
Thickly applied paint with visible texture.
Transparent layer over a dry layer to tint it.
Painting with only a few chosen colours.
Colours opposite on the colour wheel.

walkthroughs.body_html: Wet-on-wet blends two colours softly while both layers are still damp — perfect for skies. Dry brush drags barely-loaded bristles over the surface so only the high points of the paper catch — perfect for grass or hair.

Impasto piles paint on so brushstrokes cast their own shadows — think Van Gogh. Glazing is the opposite: a transparent thin layer over a dry one, shifting the colour underneath. Acrylic and oil both glaze well.

A limited palette (e.g. red, yellow, blue, white) forces colour harmony. A complementary palette uses opposites for maximum contrast. An analogous palette uses neighbours on the wheel for a calm, unified feel.
